message.content:
Method: Conduct a preregistered, two-stage experiment on the 111-unit array. Use pilot runs only to establish feasible settings, verify measurement reliability, and estimate variance for the run-count calculation. Do not use pilot outcomes to set confirmatory detection thresholds or to choose analysis options based on temporal-order results. Freeze the confirmatory protocol and analysis code before collecting or examining confirmatory outcomes.

In the confirmatory stage, randomize independent runs in blocks defined by experimental day to a balanced design with three coupling levels and two drive levels. Hold disorder at a measured, prespecified baseline for this primary experiment. Choose actual levels in the pilot to span distinct coarsening rates while remaining within the same operating regime. Define that regime in advance using stable actuation, bounded unit motion, and absence of transitions to qualitatively different response states. Record delivered drive, disorder, and any coupling-dependent changes in stiffness, damping, or other measurable properties. If disorder is studied, add a separately randomized, separately powered extension with its own prespecified contrasts; do not combine it with the primary analysis post hoc.

Use the same reset and equilibration procedure before every run. Before applying the experimental drive, measure displacement, phase, and spatial correlations. Define numerical tolerances for baseline comparability and exclusion before unblinding. Randomize condition order within day-level blocks and verify that resetting removes detectable carryover. Determine the number of confirmatory runs by simulation using pilot estimates of onset frequency, censoring, and between-day variation. State the target effect or confidence-interval precision, assumptions, and final run count in the preregistration.

Synchronize actuator phase, imaging, and unit-level motion or shear measurements. For each run and time point, calculate the mean-subtracted spatial correlation function along both array axes, correcting for the array’s measured finite boundaries. Fit a prespecified exponential-decay model over a fixed distance range chosen from spatial resolution and array dimensions, not from confirmatory outcomes. Define the primary correlation length as the geometric mean of the two axis-specific fitted lengths; report their ratio as the anisotropy measure. If a fit fails a preregistered goodness-of-fit or identifiability check, mark that estimate missing and report the failure rate by condition; do not substitute a different model in the primary analysis. Report sensitivity analyses using prespecified alternative fit ranges and models.

For temporal order, determine drive frequency from the measured actuator phase over each run and define the target subharmonic at half that frequency. Analyze fixed-length windows of a preregistered number of drive cycles, using a fixed taper and a fixed step in cycles. Define the subharmonic score as power in the target bin divided by the median power in preregistered neighboring bands, excluding the target bin, drive harmonics, and known resonances. Estimate phase coherence as the magnitude of the mean unit phasor after demodulating each unit’s signal at the target subharmonic, with phase referenced to the actuator and summarized across units and cycles.

Calibrate the score and coherence thresholds using null signals that preserve measured spatial and temporal dependence while disrupting stable subharmonic phase locking. Run the complete window scan on each null dataset and choose thresholds to keep the run-level probability of any false onset below the preregistered alpha level. Define onset as the first window in which both thresholds are exceeded and remain exceeded for a preregistered number of consecutive, non-overlapping drive-cycle blocks. This block rule defines persistence in drive cycles; overlapping spectral windows may be used for localization but do not count as independent persistence observations. Set the observation duration in advance using pilot onset and censoring estimates. Runs without qualifying onset are right-censored. Define persistence as time from onset to the first qualifying block in which either criterion fails for the required consecutive blocks; persistence still present at the run endpoint is right-censored.

The primary causal estimand is the difference in onset time between the lowest and highest coupling levels at the reference drive level, analyzed by intention to treat. The key secondary estimand is the corresponding difference in persistence. Estimate these with discrete-time survival models using a complementary log-log link, coupling as a prespecified categorical factor, day as a random intercept, and drive and coupling-by-drive interaction as prespecified terms. Report contrasts with confidence intervals. Control family-wise error across the two primary outcomes using a preregistered procedure; treat remaining coupling contrasts and interactions as secondary. Handle time dependence through the defined non-overlapping onset blocks, not by counting sliding windows as independent observations.

As secondary mechanistic analyses, test whether pre-onset correlation length and coarsening rate improve prediction of onset beyond randomized condition and drive. Compare three prespecified accounts: coarsening predicts order, drive predicts both observables in parallel, and temporal order precedes changes in coarsening. Compare them using blocked cross-validation by experimental day and a preregistered log predictive score. These analyses are predictive and conditional: randomized coupling estimates the effect of changing coupling, not the isolated causal effect of correlation length. Do not interpret mediation as established if coupling also changes other physical pathways.

Report all tested settings, exclusions, missing or failed spatial fits, censoring, and sensitivity to the prespecified alternative spatial models, spectral backgrounds, and thresholds. Bound conclusions to this array and the tested parameter range. To assess transferability, repeat the harmonized protocol in a separate study across array sizes and geometries, and across drive and disorder regimes. Prespecify how boundary conditions and anisotropy will be measured and how operating regimes will be matched; test empirically whether the spatial and temporal metrics remain comparable rather than assuming transfer.

Rationale: The target paper reports that wave coarsening drives time crystallization. The supplied aggregate export shows increasing correlation width and an early rise followed by relatively stable mean shear, but it lacks synchronized raw signals and run identifiers. It therefore cannot establish subharmonic order, temporal precedence, run-level variability, or causality. Its 2,199 time samples are not independent experimental replicates, and the exported width uncertainty does not specify the underlying aggregation. The export motivates the follow-up question but cannot answer it.

The randomized coupling contrast tests whether changing coupling changes coarsening and temporal-order onset at fixed drive and disorder. The drive factor distinguishes that effect from a direct or parallel drive response. Explicit estimands, baseline checks, fit-failure rules, dependence-preserving null calibration, and a cycle-based onset definition address the remaining operational ambiguities and make the analysis reproducible. Requiring both spectral power and phase coherence, with calibrated run-level false-onset control, reduces the risk of mistaking finite-window fluctuations or ordinary drive responses for robust temporal order.

A coupling effect on onset would support a causal effect of the coupling intervention in the tested regime, but would not prove that correlation length is the sole mechanism. Predictive model comparisons can assess whether coarsening adds explanatory value and whether its timing is consistent with the competing accounts; they remain secondary evidence because coupling may affect temporal order through other pathways. Generalization beyond the 111-unit array requires direct replication across geometries, sizes, and operating regimes.
